rooms.long: An open grave where a small city once thrived.
A fractured gatehouse leans over the road, its doors long gone. Wind moves through the empty arch where iron once hung.

Deep ruts crease the old street, packed with silt and stray grass. Collapsed
curbs and leaning posts hint at buildings beyond the weeds.

Broken stones show where wheels once cut a track through the city. Old gutter
stones run broken and half buried at the sides.

Loose gravel and dirt bury the street's edge. Low foundations crouch in the
weeds, their doorways open to the air.

A low ring of stone marks a circle at the center of the road. Whatever stood
here is gone, leaving only shattered plinths.

Water has eaten shallow channels along the roadbed. Windblown dust gathers in
the ruts where traffic once passed.

Weeds press up through the cracked paving stones. Small stones and splinters
of brick mark where walls fell.

The street lies uneven, its stones tilted and split. Vines trail across the
road in slow, careless loops.

Ruts and puddled clay mark the old path between low walls. Scattered rubble
suggests a long abandoned block.

Thin grass grows in the grooves left by carts. Loose brick and fallen beams
dot the edges of the street.

Dry mud fills the depressions in the street. Thistles and briars knot along
the broken verge.

Two worn streets cross in a patch of sunken stone. The corners are choked with
rubble from nearby walls.

A broad civic hall slumps behind a fallen portico. Its doors gape open onto
dust and broken benches.

A small plaza opens between low buildings, its paving split by weeds. A dry
fountain basin lies cracked at its center.

A broad road runs between fractured curbstones and toppled markers. The center
is worn smooth where traffic once passed.

A narrow storefront sits silent, its signboard fallen into the street. The
interior is stripped and open to weather.

Old paving stones show through a blanket of dust and grit. Grass collects
along the edges in long seams.

The road runs straight between broken foundations. Dust and grit have buried
the old curb.

The roadbed dips where the ground has settled. Broken walls crowd close on
either side.

A long stretch of road lies quiet under a thin scatter of leaves. The gutters
are choked with soil and moss.

Cracked paving gives way to patches of dirt and gravel. A few stones still
hold the line of the old curb.

The road narrows and loses its paving in a drift of soil. Beyond it, the track
dissolves into grass.
A narrow lane begins between sagging houses. The stones are uneven and broken.

A narrow lane winds between close houses with shuttered windows. Damp stains
stripe the stone.

The lane runs straight between close walls streaked with damp. A thin line of
grass follows the center.

The lane is quiet and tight, its paving broken in places. Moss spreads along
the base of each wall.

The lane ends at a collapsed wall and a heap of stone. The path beyond has
faded into dirt.

Tall facades begin along the street, their windows hollow. The paving here is
cleaner, though still cracked.

Tall facades line the street, their balconies empty. Old banners have left
pale marks on the stone.

A formal row of buildings rises in matched stone. Windows stare out as dark,
broken squares.

Wide steps front each entrance, all worn to hollows. Rain has streaked the
carved lintels.

The street feels ceremonial, though no one walks it now. Even the paving here
is fractured and dull.

A round shaft drops into darkness, its rim lined with broken stone. Cold air
pools at the mouth and carries the scent of damp earth.

A small guard niche sits beside the street, its roof fallen in. A rusted bell
lies in the debris.

A heavy round door stands in a curved wall, swollen and cracked by time. Moss
gathers in the seams where the frame once fit tight.

A yard of scattered metal and broken carts sprawls between low fences. Rusted
frames and bent tools lie half buried in dirt.

A narrow archway divides the street, flanked by low guard niches. The stone
bears faint carvings worn flat by time.

The line of grand facades fades into a broken cul-de-sac. A fallen wall spills
into the street, blocking the far end.

The alley narrows to a dead end cluttered with collapsed beams. Damp stains
run down the brick where rooflines failed.

The alley turns around a sagging corner where bricks have slipped. Loose
stones and soot gather along the base.

A tight bend hides the alley from the street, keeping it dark and stale. The
walls are pocked with old nail holes and cracks.

This passage is hemmed by close walls and a broken gutter. Thin weeds reach up
from packed dirt.

The alley lies in permanent shade, its stones damp and uneven. Refuse has long
since rotted into the cracks.

A narrow opening splits the row of buildings, leading into shadow. The lintel
above is cracked and sagging.

A heavy door and shuttered windows mark a hall that was once important. The
sign above the entrance hangs broken and unreadable.

A wide entry hall stands open to the street, swept by dust. Torn curtains hang
from a balcony that no longer shelters the floor.

A low room of tables and a cracked bar lies silent. Dull glass and dry spills
stain the floor.

Wide steps lead up to a carved facade streaked with rain. The doorway stands
open, its lintel chipped and scarred.

The street widens slightly here before narrowing into ruins. Broken shutters
and beams lie along the verge.

A straight street runs between low walls and empty storefronts. Loose grit
crunches over the paving.

The street here is broad, its stones worn smooth in places. Small piles of
rubble mark fallen doorways.

Cracked paving leads past shuttered houses with sagging roofs. Grass grows in
a thin line along the middle.

A narrow stone bridge spans a shallow, weed-choked channel. Several stones are
missing, leaving gaps that show the water below.

The bridge arches over a dry channel, its sides worn smooth. Moss gathers
along the parapet where hands once rested.

A stretch of street opens toward a cluster of ruined roofs. Shadows gather
where eaves once held light.

The stone street runs toward a tangle of fallen masonry. Its edges are
softened by drifted soil and grass.

A low guard post slumps beside the road, its roof fallen in. The doorway is
filled with debris.

Broken statues stand amid tall grass, their faces worn away. Plinths sit
cracked and empty where others fell.

A lawn once trimmed is now wild, dotted with shattered stone figures. Moss
coats the remaining bases.

What was once a tended lawn is now a mat of tall grass. Stone borders still
trace its careful shape.

A high entry hall opens beneath a cracked vault. Dust lies deep where
footsteps once echoed.

This chamber holds a chill that lingers year round. Frost clings to the stone
in thin, pale sheets.

A narrow hall carries the breath of cold stone. The floor is slick with old
moisture.

Snow has drifted into a hollow chamber, piled in soft ridges. Bare rock shows
through where the wind has scoured.

A broken gate stands ajar in a high wall, its hinges rusted solid. The
courtyard beyond lies empty and windblown.

A plain foyer opens onto several doorways, each stripped of its doors. The
ceiling has darkened with age.

Wood panels line the hall, warped and split by damp. Their varnish has dulled
to a gray sheen.

A long hearth sits cold beneath a soot-dark hood. Cracked tables and empty
shelves crowd the room.

Fragments of wall stand like ribs around a roofless room. The open sky looks
down on rubble and weeds.

A heavy bridge spans a shallow moat now filled with reed and mud. Chains hang
slack where the lift once rose.

An arched entry stands flanked by shattered shelves. Damp paper lies in curled
fragments on the stone.

Round cobbles form the hall floor, slick with age. The walls narrow as the
corridor stretches on.

The hallway bends around a thick pillar, hiding what lies beyond. Dust gathers
in the corner where the light fades.

A narrow cell holds a bare cot frame and a low shelf. The stone is cold and
damp.

This small chamber is plain, its walls marked by soot and smoke. A slit window
admits a thin stripe of light.

A massive door hangs from one hinge, leaving a gap into the dark. Rust and rot
have eaten the frame.

A cobbled corridor runs straight beneath a low ceiling. Water has darkened the
stones near the edges.

A cramped room opens off the hall, empty of comforts. Scratches line the wall
where wood once hung.

A gentle turn shifts the corridor toward colder air. The floor stones are
chipped and uneven.

The cell is spare and silent, its floor worn smooth. Moisture beads on the
corners.

This narrow shop is lined with empty hooks and dark stains. The air is stale
and sweet with old rot.

A once-lively tavern sits dim behind broken windows. A sagging stage and
splintered stools fill the corners.

A grand hall stands stripped to bare stone, banners long gone. Ash marks a
hearth that has not burned in years.

A weathered board stands against the wall, its notices long since torn away.
Rusted nails hold scraps of curled parchment.

The park path begins among low shrubs and toppled benches. Grass has pushed
through the paving stones.

Two narrow paths cross under a thinning canopy. Fallen limbs lie where the
walkways once met cleanly.

Tiny stone markers jut from the earth in uneven lines. Many have tipped over
or sunk into the soil.

The path climbs a low rise where the ground is bare and windy. A line of trees
leans over the slope.

This path runs along a raised embankment of cracked stone. The drop to either
side is softened by weeds.

The path ends at a low wall broken into piles of stone. Beyond it, the park
gives way to rough ground.

Broken columns and a fallen altar mark the remains of a temple. Vines trail
through the shattered roofline.

A circular chamber rises around a cracked dome. Light spills through gaps
where the roof has fallen.

A gravel path winds toward a distant, pale structure. Pebbles crunch in the
wind where weeds have not taken hold.

The gravel path climbs a slope scattered with loose stone. It narrows where
the hill has begun to slip.

Gravel paths meet in a small clearing of trampled stone. One branch is almost
lost beneath grass.

A pale manor stands behind a tangle of dead hedges. Its walls are stained and
its windows are blind.

An iron gate hangs open on one hinge, set in a low stone wall. The ground
beyond is uneven with old graves.

A simple post of stone stands abandoned at the corner. Only a cracked bench
remains inside.

A broader road begins near a low wall of fallen stone. The surface is cracked
but still passable.

The road is scarred with shallow ruts and missing stones. Wind has piled grit
against the surviving curb.

A tall gate of dark iron stands between two cracked pillars. The metal is
pitted and flecked with rust.

A square of broken paving holds the meeting of several paths. The stones are
sunken and split by roots.

A narrower walk skirts a line of study halls. The stones are uneven and
spotted with moss.

The path runs beside a low wall, its capstones cracked. Weeds crowd the base
where soil has risen.

A low structure of rough boards leans at a tired angle. Its roof has caved in
along one side.

Half-built walls stand around a pit of shattered stone. Tools and braces have
long since rotted away.

A small dining room opens into a bare kitchen. The counters are bare and the
hearth is cold.

The base of a watchtower opens into shadow beneath a cracked arch. Old arrows
and stones lie scattered outside.

A stone walk runs between broad buildings with blank windows. Leaves gather in
shallow drifts along the edges.

The path is straight and formal, though its stones have shifted. Silent
facades rise on both sides.

A short railing borders a narrow entry in the wall. The iron bars are bent and
mottled with rust.

Flat stones form a short entry that has sunk into the ground. Weeds push
through every seam.

A low wall encloses a yard gone to weeds. A warped signpost leans among the
grass.

A plain foyer opens into several small chambers. Dust lies thick where beds
once stood.

Long tables stand in a wide hall, their surfaces split and gray. A cold hearth
sits at the far end.

Cracked paving leads past a row of empty doorways. Grass pushes up where the
joints have widened.

A long walk stretches across a quiet quadrangle. The air is still beneath
tall, weathered walls.

The path narrows where rubble has spilled from a broken stair. Dust and grit
soften the once-sharp edges.

A formal walkway continues between shuttered halls. Only wind and birds move
among the stones.

Rows of benches face a high dais in a broad hall. The floor is scuffed by
long-quiet feet.

A modest office holds a cracked desk and empty shelves. The window shutters
hang loose on their hinges.

An unfinished foundation lies open to the weather. Broken scaffolds lean where
they were left.

A narrow office holds a broken chair and a faded ledger. The walls are stained
where lamps once burned.

A stone entry opens into a building of long worktables. The lintel is etched
with worn markings.

Long tables and rusted tools line the walls. A few cracked vessels still rest
on their shelves.

Stepped benches rise in a semicircle, all coated with dust. A cracked slate
stands at the front.

A gravel path winds between scrub and low stone walls. Small stones shift with
any movement.

Vines curtain a low arch, their roots wedged into the stone. The entry beyond
is dim and cool.

A tall foyer rises toward a broken skylight. Bits of colored glass glitter in
the dust.

Loose gravel crunches along a narrow path. The ground beside it is soft with
moss.

A low room sits tucked under a stair, its walls scratched and scuffed. A toy
chest lies smashed in a corner.

A hallway lined with wooden beams runs between stone walls. The boards are
warped and dark with age.

Hanging vines trail through a low entry into a row of small rooms. The floor
is littered with leaves and dust.

A small room opens onto a broken balcony above the ground. The ceiling is
stained with rain.

Flat stones form a narrow path, each one tilted and cracked. Grass grows thick
between the joints.

A gray stone foyer holds a cold stillness. Damp stains stripe the walls from
floor to lintel.

A small office holds a counting table and empty shelves. The shutters are
cracked and hang ajar.

A wide shed holds the outlines of old stalls. The roof has gaps where light
falls through.

A low-ceilinged room is divided into narrow cubbies. The partitions are warped
and splintered.

Thick stone columns flank the entry to a broad hall. Their carvings are worn
smooth.

A squat tower rises above the wall, its stairs broken. The top is open to rain
and birds.

A suite of rooms lies empty beyond a carved doorway. Dust lies in drifts where
rugs once lay.

Large vats sit rusted in a cool chamber. The floor is sticky with old spills
and mold.

A square office holds a heavy desk and a cracked seal. The walls bear faint
marks of old banners.

Empty racks line the walls, their pegs snapped off. A few rusted scraps lie in
the corners.

The base of a windmill stands open to the wind, its beams creaking. Grain dust
has long settled into the floor.

Rusting frames and gears sit half swallowed by vines. A path winds between
them in silence.

Graves spread across a low field, their markers tilted and worn. The ground is
uneven with sunken plots.

A cramped workroom holds tiny benches and cracked tools. The walls are
blackened by old smoke.

A heavy room holds idle mechanisms, their belts long rotted away. Oil stains
and rust mark the floor.
